messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Teams: Retirement of off-network invitations to Teams Free
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Teams will retire off-network invitations for Teams Free accounts starting December 2026. Users can no longer invite external people via email or chat links to create Teams Free accounts. Existing Teams Free collaboration and federation remain unchanged. No admin action is needed, but user guidance should be updated.
messageCenterItems.body:
What and Why:

Microsoft Teams will retire the invitation flow that allows work or school users to invite people who cannot be found in Teams to create a Teams Free account and join a chat. This change retires the off-network invitation flow (via email or sharing a link to chat) only — not federation with Teams Free.

Rollout Schedule:

Worldwide: We will begin rolling out in early December 2026 and expect to complete by late December 2026.

Impact on Your Organization:

Who is affected:

  • Users who use the off-network email invitation flow to invite external people to create a Teams Free account and join a chat.
  • Users who user share a link to chat flow to invite external people to create a Teams Free account and join a chat. 

Platforms/Services:

  • Microsoft Teams desktop, web and mobile apps

What will happen:

  • Users will no longer be able to send these onboarding invitations from Teams chats.
  • People who need a Teams Free account will need to create one independently or collaborate through another supported method.
  • Collaboration with existing Teams Free users remains available, subject to your organization's external-access policies.
  • This change will take effect automatically. No admin action is required to enable the retirement.

Action Required/Recommendations:

No admin action is required for this change to take effect. However, we recommend updating user guidance and helpdesk documentation before December 6, 2026, to reflect the following alternatives:

  • For ongoing chat: If recipients do not have a Teams account, they can create a Teams Free account independently or get invited as guests to an existing team. Once their account is discoverable, users can search for their registered email address and start a conversation.
  • For team and channel collaboration: No change.
  • For meetings: No change.

Compliance considerations:

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Teams: Users can temporarily pause all notifications
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Teams will allow users to temporarily pause notifications for a chosen duration to reduce interruptions and improve focus. This feature, available on desktop, web, and mobile, rolls out globally from mid-September to November 2026. No admin action is needed; users can enable it via their profile menu.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated November 10, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

What and Why:

Microsoft Teams will introduce a new capability that allows users to temporarily pause notifications for a selected period of time. This feature gives users greater control over interruptions, helps reduce notification overload, and enables focused work, meetings, and other activities without requiring changes to existing notification settings.

Rollout Schedule:

  • Targeted Release (Worldwide): Rollout begins in mid-September 2026 and is expected to complete by early October 2026.
  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Rollout begins in early October 2026 and is expected to complete by end November 2026 (previously late October).

Impact on Your Organization:

Who is affected:

  • All Microsoft Teams users.

Platforms:

  • Microsoft Teams desktop, web, and mobile.

What will happen:

  • Users will be able to temporarily pause Teams notifications for a selected duration.
  • The feature helps users focus on important work and meetings without modifying their existing notification settings.
  • Users can access this capability from the profile menu in the upper-right corner of the Teams application.
  • Once the selected pause period ends, notifications will automatically resume using the user's existing notification preferences.

Action Required/Recommendations:

No admin action is required.

Consider informing users about this new capability so they can take advantage of improved notification management and reduced distractions while maintaining their existing notification preferences.

Compliance Considerations:

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Teams: Malicious QR code detection in messages
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Teams will detect malicious QR codes in messages starting mid-November 2026, warning users of harmful links. Detection applies to chats and channels, with external QR codes blurred by default. The feature is enabled via existing Malicious URL protection, requiring no admin action.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated November 10, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

What and why

Microsoft Teams is extending malicious URL protection to provide near-real-time detection of malicious destinations embedded in QR codes shared in messages. Teams will analyze QR code destinations to identify potential phishing and fraud threats and display an additional warning when malicious content is detected.

Rollout schedule

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in mid-November 2026 (previously early November) and expected to complete by late November 2026 (previously mid-November)

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Users who use Microsoft Teams messaging

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams chats, meeting chats, and channels

What will happen

  • Teams will decode and evaluate QR code destinations in inline images shared in 1:1 chats, group chats, meeting chats, and channels.
  • Detection applies to internal and external communications.
  • Images containing QR codes from external senders are already blurred by default. When Teams identifies a malicious QR code, users will also see the warning, “This message contains a link that might be harmful,” and a “Learn about file and link safety” link.
  • QR code images from internal senders are not blurred by default. The same warning will appear when Teams detects a malicious QR code.
  • For users on Teams mobile in China, QR code images are blurred by default regardless of whether the sender is internal or external, and any messages containing malicious QR code will be blocked.
  • Malicious QR code detection is managed by the existing Malicious URL protection setting.
  • The setting is enabled by default. Organizations with Malicious URL protection enabled will automatically receive malicious QR code detection as the feature rolls out.
  • No separate configuration is available or required for malicious QR code detection.

Action required and recommendations

No admin action is required.

Admins can review or change the existing Malicious URL protection setting in Teams admin center > Settings and policies > Messaging Safety.

We recommend that you:

  • Inform users and help desk staff about the additional warning for detected malicious QR codes.
  • Clarify that QR code blurring is a separate precautionary experience and does not mean that Teams has identified a QR code as malicious.
  • Review internal documentation about Teams messaging security and update it if necessary.

Learn more

(Both to be updated closer to rollout.)

  • Make sure chats, links, and files are secure in Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Support
  • Malicious URL protection in Microsoft Teams - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Teams: Invite attendees to register
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Teams is expanding the "Invite to register" feature for events, allowing organizers to email registration links. Rolling out worldwide by late November 2026. No special preparation needed, but configuring a custom domain for M365 notifications is recommended to avoid restrictions. No compliance issues identified.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated November 10, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

What and Why:

Microsoft Teams is expanding the Invite to register experience for Teams events with registration enabled. Organizers can select people to receive an email invitation with a link to register for the event.

Rollout Schedule:

General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): We will begin rolling out in late November 2026 (previously mid-November) and expect to complete by late November 2026.

Impact on Your Organization:

Invite to register will be available across event access types, including public, organization-wide, and events limited to specific people and groups. For public and organization-wide events, sending an invitation does not change who is eligible to register. For events limited to specific people and groups, the selected audience continues to determine registration eligibility.

This update gives organizers a consistent way to proactively invite their intended audience to register for an event.

Action Required/Recommendations:

No special preparation is required. However, if your tenant does not have a custom domain configured for M365 notifications, this capability will be restricted due to spam concerns. Admins should configure their custom domain for M365 notifications to allow full use of this feature.

Compliance considerations:

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Teams: Automatic recording and transcription options align with admin policies
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Teams will update meeting options to show automatic recording and transcription settings based on assigned policies, adding a new "Record only" option. Rollout starts mid-November 2026, completing by mid-December. No admin action is needed; organizers see only options allowed by their policies.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated November 10, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

What and why

Microsoft Teams is updating the Record and transcribe automatically setting in Meeting options, so meeting organizers see only the automatic recording and transcription options permitted by their assigned Teams meeting policies. This change reduces confusion, improves policy compliance, and helps ensure organizers cannot select options that are unavailable based on organizational settings.

As part of this update, Teams will introduce a new Record only option that automatically starts meeting recording without starting transcription.

Rollout schedule

  • Targeted Release: Beginning in mid-November 2026 (previously early November) and expected to complete by end of November 2026 (previously mid-November)
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in early December 2026 and expected to complete by mid-December 2026

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Teams administrators who manage meeting recording and transcription policies
  • Meeting organizers who configure automatic recording or transcription settings in Meeting options

Platforms and services

  • Teams desktop, web, and mobile clients that support Meeting Options.

What will happen

  • Meeting organizers will only see automatic recording and transcription options allowed by their effective Teams meeting policy.
  • Policy evaluation respects policies assigned directly to a user, inherited through group assignment, or applied through the global policy.
  • A new Record only option will be available when recording is permitted by policy.

  • The available automatic options for each policy combination are shown below:
Recording policyTranscription policyAutomatic options available in Meeting Options
AllowedAllowedRecord and transcribe; Transcribe only; Record only; Off
AllowedBlockedRecord only; Off
BlockedAllowedTranscribe only; Off
BlockedBlockedThe automatic setting is not shown

Action required and recommendations

No admin action is required; the feature is enabled automatically as part of the service update.

We recommend that:

  • Inform meeting organizers about the new Record only option.
  • Communicate that available automatic recording and transcription options are now determined by the organizer's assigned Teams meeting policies.
  • Review recording and transcription policies if you want to understand which options organizers in your organization will see.

Compliance considerations

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Teams: Video sharing from OneDrive in Teams events
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Teams will soon allow event organizers and producers to share videos directly from OneDrive during Teams events using "Manage what attendees see," enabling smoother, higher-quality playback without screen sharing or embedding in PowerPoint. Rollout begins mid-November 2026, with no action required.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated November 10, 2026: We have updated the timeline. If you are a tenant in a GCCH or DoD environment, you can safely ignore this message as you are not impacted. Thank you for your patience. 

What and why

Microsoft Teams will soon support sharing video directly from OneDrive during Teams events. Organizers and producers using Manage what attendees see can load videos from OneDrive and present them on stage without screen sharing a local media player or embedding videos in PowerPoint. This improvement provides smoother, higher-quality video playback for attendees and simplifies event production through built-in video playback controls.

Rollout schedule

  • Targeted Release (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in mid-November 2026 (previously early November) and end in early December 2026.
  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): Rollout will begin in early December 2026 and is expected to complete by early December 2026.

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Teams event organizers and producers using events configured with Manage what attendees see.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams
  • OneDrive
  • Teams events

What will happen

  • Organizers and producers will be able to select and share videos stored in OneDrive directly within Teams events configured with Manage what attendees see and will have access to built-in controls to start and pause video playback during events.
  • Videos can be presented on stage without screen sharing a local media player or embedding videos into a PowerPoint presentation.
  • Attendees will experience smoother and higher-quality video playback.

Action required and recommendations

No action is required. We recommend that you:

  • Inform Teams event organizers and producers that they can share videos directly from OneDrive in Teams events configured with Manage what attendees see.
  • Ensure that organizers and producers store videos in OneDrive with the appropriate permissions before using them in events.
  • Review and update internal event production guidance that recommends screen sharing locally played videos or embedding videos in PowerPoint.

Learn more

We will update this post with new documentation.

Compliance considerations

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.
